en: The Praise of the Lion of the Śākyas, Extracted from the Nectar of Prosody:
I bow to him who is accompanied by a multitude of monks, seated at the foot of a tree together with the Tathāgatas.
Those *upajāti* meters are those whose two feet possess the characteristics just described. || 1 ||

I bow to the Buddha, the most excellent of youths named Sarvārthasiddha, who is the graceful crest-jewel of the Śākya king’s lineage, whose radiance exceeds that of the moon and surpasses the brilliance of gold, and who is perfected through the Upajāti meter.
I perpetually bow to him whose conduct is irreproachable, who is stainless and possesses a pure bodily form;
whose mind is solely intent on uplifting all living beings, who has the face of the moon and beautiful, white lotus-feet. (3)
To the son of Śuddhodana, protected by Gautami, the son of Māyā, the conqueror of Māra, the Great One;
whose form is to be honored by Maheśvara and others, who possesses immeasurable majesty and immeasurable Dharma. || 4 ||

I bow to him who has crossed the ocean of existence, whose infinite merit is honored by the gods beginning with Bhava, who is to be meditated upon by beings of infinite potential, and whose limbs are adorned with the splendor of the worthy. (5)

The aged patriarch of the lineage, the lord of kings, spoke to the people: "Summon my son, the sovereign Jinarāja, who has defeated his enemies; six years have passed since he departed and we fell into a state of separation. (6)
Worship the Lord of Sages, the elder of the lineage, beneath a tree in the great forest on a pure spot—
He who is the welfare of the world, the one born from the side of the boon-granting Dakṣa, the mother of the universe, and the ender of birth and old age.

Praising with four faces the glorious Śākyasiṃha, who has risen like the moon from the ocean of the lineage of the Śākya lords, Brahmā, the four-faced one, attained the merit of his own four faces multiplied fourfold—how wonderful! (8)
Janārdana, the fire that consumes the lineage of the lords of the Daityas, having offered his joined palms to the lotus-seated Brahmā with both hands,
touched the four arms of the Four-armed One, thinking, "I have attained double the merit."
The hymn to the glorious Śākyasiṃha, extracted from the Amṛta, is completed.
